title: Transitioning from TinyML to Edge GenAI: A Review
content:
Generative AI (GenAI) models are designed to produce realistic and natural data, such 1
as images, audio, or written text. Due to their high computational and memory demands, these 2
models traditionally run on powerful remote compute servers. However, there is growing interest 3
in deploying GenAI models at the edge, on resource-constrained embedded devices. Since 2018, 4
the TinyML community has proved that running fixed topology AI models on edge devices offers 5
several benefits, including independence from the Internet connectivity, low-latency processing, and 6
enhanced privacy. Nevertheless, deploying resource-consuming GenAI models on embedded devices 7
is challenging since the latter have limited computational, memory, and energy resources. This review 8
paper aims to evaluate the progresses made to date in the field of Edge GenAI, an emerging area of 9
research within the broader domain of EdgeAI which focuses on bringing GenAI on edge devices. 10
Papers released between 2022 and 2024 that addressed the design and deployment of GenAI models 11
on embedded devices have been identified and described. Additionally, their approaches and results 12
have been compared. This manuscript contributes to understand the ongoing transition from TinyML 13
to Edge GenAI and provides valuable insights to the AI research community on this emerging and 14
impactful, quite under-explored field.
